title: The Secret Space Fence That Detected Something Moving Faster Than Light
hook: A classified radar system designed to track space debris picked up an object that broke the laws of physics—and then the feed was cut.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines conspiracy appeal with hard physics violation, creating immediate skepticism and urge to understand.

title: The Star That Vanished—And Left a Perfect Void in Its Place
hook: Astronomers watched a star disappear in real time, but where it should have been, there was nothing—no debris, no black hole, just absence.
why_this_can_go_viral: Violates expectation of stellar death, feels like a cosmic magic trick that terrifies.

title: The Dark Matter Signal That Caused a Scientist to Quit in Terror
hook: A researcher monitoring a dark matter detector saw a pattern that made him walk out and never speak about it again.
why_this_can_go_viral: Personal trauma from scientific discovery creates mystery and questions about what was seen.

title: The Classified Apollo Mission That Found a Structure on the Dark Side
hook: Declassified audio reveals astronauts discussing a geometric object on the far side of the moon—and then ordering radio silence.
why_this_can_go_viral: Moon base theories never die; adding 'radio silence' triggers deep distrust in space agencies.

title: The Rogue Planet That Carried a Signal From a Dead Civilization
hook: A planet drifting alone between stars emitted a repeating radio pattern that matches no natural source. The message is a warning.
why_this_can_go_viral: Combines loneliness of interstellar space with the terror of receiving a warning you can't decode.

title: The Black Hole That Exists in a Different Dimension—And Leaks Into Ours
hook: Data from the Event Horizon Telescope shows something emerging from a black hole that shouldn't be possible—a structure from another plane.
why_this_can_go_viral: Multiverse and higher dimensions fascinate; the 'leak' implies danger.

title: The Secret Soviet Program That Detected a Return Signal From the Void
hook: In 1988, a Soviet radio telescope aimed at empty space received a reply. The message was in Russian. From nowhere.
why_this_can_go_viral: Nationalistic twist + impossible reply creates a chilling closed-loop mystery.

title: The Dark Matter Cloud That Made a Town Go Blind for Three Days
hook: A Peruvian village lost sight for 72 hours after a dark matter fluctuation passed overhead. Doctors found no physical cause.
why_this_can_go_viral: Real documented mass hysteria with a cosmic culprit that can't be disproven easily.

title: The Star That Sent a Binary Message—And Someone Answered Before We Did
hook: A star pulsing in perfect binary code caught our attention. But when we checked the logs, a reply had already been sent. Not by us.
why_this_can_go_viral: Someone else speaking for humanity is an existential shock; implies hidden contact.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That Swallowed a Space Probe—And It Still Transmits
hook: A deep space probe went silent after crossing an anomaly. Years later, its signal returned—from inside a black hole, still transmitting data.
why_this_can_go_viral: Transmission from beyond event horizon violates known physics—captures imagination.

title: The Extinction Event That Was a Targeted Attack—The Evidence Is in the Crater
hook: The Chicxulub impactor wasn't random. The angle, speed, and composition suggest it was aimed. Someone wanted dinosaurs dead.
why_this_can_go_viral: Rewrites a known event as an assassination, triggering survival paranoia.

title: The Fermi Paradox Filter That Reprograms Life Into Silence
hook: Every civilization that reaches a certain technological level goes quiet. Not because they die—but because something makes them forget to speak.
why_this_can_go_viral: Dark twist on Fermi—we're not alone, we're just being muted.

title: The Comet That Cracked Open—And Released Something That Moved on Its Own
hook: A comet broke apart near Jupiter, releasing a dark mass that changed trajectory independently. It was alive. And it came this way.
why_this_can_go_viral: Alien life as a hidden entity inside comets is primal horror.

title: The Classified Telescope That Saw a Face in the Cosmic Microwave Background
hook: A Soviet satellite scanning the CMB returned an image that looks like a face—billions of years old—staring at Earth from the dawn of time.
why_this_can_go_viral: Face in the oldest light implies the universe is watching us.

title: The Star That Erupted in a Pattern That Matched Human DNA
hook: A stellar flare sequence matched the base pair sequence of human DNA with 99.8% accuracy. Either coincidence—or origin.
why_this_can_go_viral: Suggests we were seeded or designed by a star, merging genetics with cosmic scale.

title: The Dark Matter Planet That Causes Gravity to Flip Every 17 Years
hook: A gravitational anomaly in the outer solar system suggests a dark matter planet that inverts gravity—and it's approaching.
why_this_can_go_viral: Gravity inversion is viscerally terrifying and uniquely clickable.

title: The Rogue Planet That's Covered in Perfectly Spherical Holes
hook: A planet in interstellar space has millions of identical spherical craters. Not impact craters. Something drilled them with precision.
why_this_can_go_viral: Geometry in nature suggests intelligence; spheres imply industrial activity.

title: The Secret NASA Program That Recorded Screams From the Van Allen Belts
hook: Radiation belt probes picked up plasma waves that, when translated to audio, sound exactly like human screams. NASA classified the data.
why_this_can_go_viral: Audio evidence of 'screaming space' is pure viral horror material.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer That Was a Census of Dead Civilizations
hook: A signal we decoded turned out to be a list of coordinates. Each one points to a planet with ruins. There are 7,842 entries.
why_this_can_go_viral: Mass extinction dataset as a message is deeply chilling and implies we're next on the list.
